overview.oneLineTake: SpaceX buys the tape a calmer open, but with credit stress and Tesla and Meta still ahead, keep short premium defined risk and lean on index rather than single name exposure.
themes: Rotation, not a tech rally. The Dow closed about 500 points higher Tuesday while the Nasdaq gave back its gains, so QQQ slipped 0.1% to 717.63 and SPY rose 0.3% to 769.05, with big banks leading and communications and tech lagging.
SpaceX lifted the after hours tape. Revenue doubled and profit beat as AI demand surged, futures rose, and Supermicro jumped on a surprise update, with Dell and HPE following.
Rates eased but stay restrictive. The 10-year was 5.15% on Monday and moved lower Tuesday after weak housing data, while hike talk stays live and homebuyers cancel at near record rates.
Oil reversed lower on hopes for Middle East diplomacy, though United cut its 2026 profit outlook on fuel and the UK is sending fighter jets to defend Saudi cities.
Earnings dispersion is wide. GM beat and narrowed guidance, Netflix beat but fell on ad and revenue guidance, and Tesla and Meta are next.
risks: AI debt issuance pushing credit swaps to new highs while equity buyers move on.
Tesla and Meta disappointing on AI spending and stalling the chip bounce.
Renewed Houthi strikes sending Brent back toward $110.
French unrest, with troops deploying ahead of more protests this weekend.

nq.regime: Range, event-driven into Tesla and Meta
nq.summary: NDX gave back Monday's gains as money rotated into banks and the Dow, with QQQ -0.1% against SPY +0.3%. SpaceX's blowout quarter lifted the after hours tape, but NQ has faded toward its session low and AI bubble talk is building. Thesis: Neutral, 4/10, range trade, fade 29,712 to 29,789 and buy confirmed holds of 29,461. Invalidation: NDX close above 29,823; risk is oil headlines lifting yields. NDX levels: resistance 29,712 (Tue high), 29,789 (Mon high), 29,823 (Fri high); support 29,461 (Mon low), 29,209 (Tue low), 29,073 (Fri low).
nq.primaryCatalyst: UK CPI 1:00 PM BKK (f 3.4%, p 3.1%); BOE Governor Bailey 8:00 PM BKK; no major US data. Tesla and Meta earnings on deck.
nq.primaryRisk: Elevated: oil headlines lifting yields; losing 29,461 NDX opens a retest of 29,209 then 29,073.
nq.overnight: NQ slipped from 29,978 to 29,859, near the session low. Oil reversed lower on Middle East diplomacy hopes; Iran rejected a report that a deal is close. NQ futures 29,868 (high 29,978 / low 29,859).
nq.macro: 10Y eased to 5.12% from 5.14% after weak housing starts, giving NQ multiples some air, but hike talk keeps a ceiling on it. DXY 101.78.
nq.volatility: VIX 17.3 (-6.1%); VXN 25.6 (Monday). Event vol held into megacap prints. Dealer gamma unavailable.

intelligence.headline: Chipmakers Lead Korean Stock Selloff on Yield Spike, IPO Stumble
intelligence.summary: The Kospi has plunged almost 40% from its June all-time high, including 3.7% today, with Samsung and SK Hynix, almost half the index's market value, down 40% and 56% since the peak despite trading at under five and under four times earnings.

intelligence.headline: Data-Center Firm Elice Plunges 32% in Seoul Debut
intelligence.summary: Elice's 32% first-day drop underscores concern about whether the AI boom justifies the billions of dollars being poured into the industry.

intelligence.headline: Stocks Weighed by IPO Flop as Bonds Gain on Haven Demand
intelligence.summary: The disappointing IPO is weighing on sentiment toward stocks more broadly, while bond prices are ticking higher as investors seek havens.

intelligence.headline: Emerging Stocks Trade at Their Biggest Ever Discount to US
intelligence.summary: The MSCI Emerging Markets Index, heavily weighted to Samsung, SK Hynix and TSMC, trades below nine times earnings; earnings from Meta, Microsoft and Alphabet this week and next could show whether the data-center spending spree has longer to run.

intelligence.headline: Japan's 20-Year Bond Sale Sees Strongest Demand on Record
intelligence.summary: Record demand at the 20-year auction signals elevated yields are starting to lure domestic investors back into the market.

intelligence.headline: Nscale, Anthropic in Talks for $45 Billion Cloud Computing Deal
intelligence.summary: AI cloud company Nscale is in talks to sell computing power to Anthropic in a deal that could be worth about $45 billion.

intelligence.headline: Ryanair CEO Predicts Highest Air Fares in History Next Year
intelligence.summary: Michael O'Leary predicted a record increase in European air fares next year as the Middle East war drives up oil prices.

intelligence.headline: On the Move: 3M Up on Amazon Deal, Apple Downgraded, Steel Dynamics Misses
intelligence.summary: Premarket: 3M +4.4% on an expanded Amazon data-center deal, Apple -0.5% on a Loop Capital downgrade to hold, Steel Dynamics -6.1% on a Q3 miss, Crown Holdings -5% on its forecast, Tradeweb +2.9% on its roughly $2 billion Trumid deal.

intelligence.headline: Earnings Today: GE, RTX, GM Before the Bell; SpaceX, Netflix After
intelligence.summary: GE, RTX, Northrop Grumman, 3M, General Motors, Halliburton and Synchrony report before the open; SpaceX, Netflix, Intuitive Surgical, Chubb, Capital One and United Airlines after the close.

intelligence.headline: Netflix Needs Blockbusters to Reverse Its $135 Billion Wipeout
intelligence.summary: Netflix is down 26% in 2026, among the 10 worst Nasdaq 100 performers and on track for its biggest annual drop since 2022, as engagement stalls on a lack of popular content; investors will watch its content pipeline in tonight's results.

intelligence.headline: AI's Advance Has FX Market Asking Whether Governance Can Keep Up
intelligence.summary: The international body that coordinates currency market standards is debating how to keep pace with AI's rapid advance.

intelligence.headline: Chile's Copper Mining Recession Deepens Amid Boom
intelligence.summary: Chile supplies 20% of global mined copper, and its aging mines have been battered by accidents, weather and missteps, which could cut output just as data-center and grid demand accelerates.
